messages:
alex: Heads-up — noticed a spike of preemptible evictions in us-west-2 during the autoscaler resize at ~07:12 UTC. Streaming clients lost ~2-3s of token stream and some requests failed. Thinking we need a graceful cutover pattern.

maria: Can you paste the evict logs? are these GCP preemptions or AWS spot?

alex: GCP preemptible; ops-bot posted the event. Logs show `SIGTERM` 30s before VM disappears. We need to avoid dropping open streams.

ops-bot: [alert] preemptible-eviction us-west2 07:11:58 — affected: gpu-pool-spot-7 (60 instances)

samir: Proposal: on SIGTERM start a "handoff window" — stop accepting new streaming sessions on spot nodes, mark existing sessions for checkpoint & requeue. Clients get a control-frame to reconnect to fallback.

kai: +1. For token streaming, do a cutover: send final "checkpoint token" row, flush KV cache, return a short control message like `{"action":"cutover","target":"ondemand"}` so client switches to ondemand websocket.

maria: How long for checkpoint? we typically see ~20-50ms per KV flush but for long prompts it might be bigger.

samir: We'll chunk checkpoints per N generated tokens and persist last 2k tokens cache to S3/redis. On reconnect, server resumes KV and replay.

lina: We should also support server-side requeue: if client can't reconnect quickly, the runtime can re-queue incomplete request to an ondemand host and continue generating, then push the remaining stream.

alex: Important to bound cost — we shouldn't requeue everything to ondemand by default. Suggest policy: requeue if remaining tokens > 64 or latency SLO would break.

kai: Example cutover pseudo:

```
on SIGTERM:
  node.status = DRAINING
  for stream in active_streams:
    send_control(stream, '{"type":"checkpoint","cursor":cur_pos}')
    persist_kv(stream.id, snapshot)
    if remaining_tokens > REQUEUE_THRESHOLD:
      enqueue_to(pool="ondemand", metadata=snapshot)
    else:
      send_final_chunk_and_close(stream)
```

maria: Also add a small penalty budget — allow X% of streaming traffic to be proactively served on ondemand during risky windows (resize, high spot churn).

samir: We need client contract changes: client must support `control` frames and reconnect URI in 5-10s. Add small backoff jitter.

lina: Ops: can we tag instances with `spot-risk` to trigger early draining before provider SIGTERM? Use ASG lifecycle hooks + preemption notice watchers.

ops-bot: [note] gcp preemption-notice endpoint fired for gpu-pool-spot-7 07:11:43 — 25s before SIGTERM.

alex: Good catch. So timeline: preemption notice -> 25s -> SIGTERM -> 30s -> eviction. Means we have ~25s to checkpoint and requeue.

maria: Tests: chaos run simulating preemptive notices with load; measure p99 token loss, reconnect success rate. If >1% failure, fallback to a conservative routing policy.

kai: Also clever idea: maintain a small warm ondemand pool to accept instant cutover (keep 5-10 warm GPUs). Cost vs reliability tradeoff.

samir: For implementation I'll add: graceful-drain handler, `requeue-request` API, control-frame schema, and metrics: `eviction.cutover.success_rate`, `eviction.requeued.count`, `eviction.tokens_lost`.

lina: I'll update runbook and add playbook steps for oncall: manual cutover toggle, force drain tag.

alex: I'll open a small RFC and a spike PR for the handler + client control frames. Thanks all :thumbsup: 

maria: :thumbsup: 

kai: lgtm, assign to samir + devex for client docs.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] created branch `eviction-cutover/sam` and CI started.
